content_of_post_to_comment:
I spent too much time trying to build the perfect morning routine.

Wake up at 6, don't touch my phone, drink water, workout, read, journal, plan the day. I do it for 3 or 4 days and feel pretty good about it then if have one late night and whole thing would go to shit. I'd wake up tired, grab my phone, skip workout, start checking stuff and suddenly it was 8:30 and I was already behind.

Then I tell myself I'd start again Monday. Kept changing morning routine thinking maybe I just hadn't found the right one yet. Different wake up time, different habits, sometimes I'd add even more stuff to try.

After a while I noticed what I was doing the night before. I'd finish whatever I was doing around 10 or 10:30, get into bed with my phone and tell myself I'd scroll for a few minutes. Then I'd be scrolling socials and somehow it was 11:30. I put the phone down realize I needed to sleep then pick it up again 5 minutes later.

Some nights I'd be doing this until midnight even though I was already tired.

The nights that actually went well were usually pretty boring. I'd leave my phone on my desk instead of taking it into bed, get my clothes ready, clean up my desk a little and write down what I needed to do first the next morning. Nothing extra ordinary.

Getting the phone out of the bedroom made a pretty big difference. If it was next to my bed, I'd usually check it. If it was across the room, I was much more likely to just go to sleep.

I still have nights where I screw this up. I get stuck watching something or scrolling and suddenly it's later than I wanted. But I don't spend the next morning trying to force myself through some huge routine anymore.

Most mornings now are just get up, get ready, coffee then start whatever I wrote down the night before. It's a lot less exciting than the routines I used to make for myself but at least I am still doing it few weeks later.
